title: Observability canary + smoke test suite for VPC/on‑prem (tf modules)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a lightweight canary + smoke-test suite to validate observability stacks in private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). Target is a repeatable terraform-driven flow that teams can run pre- and post-upgrade to catch integration regressions (metrics, alerts, dashboards, log egress, OTEL pipelines).

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Verify Prometheus ingestion and retention behaviour for tenant namespaces.
- Validate Grafana dashboards render expected panels and datasource connectivity.
- Confirm OTEL Collector pipelines accept local OTLP and forward to configured backends (prometheus remote write, grafana tempo, log sink).
- Smoke-test log shipping path to S3/Kafka/HTTP sink used in the deployment.
- Validate alert firing and pager path (pagerduty webhook -> relay) in an isolated test channel.
- Provide terraform module knobs for customers to self-run canaries in their VPC without full infra churn.

High-level approach:
1) Terraform module: observability-canary.
   - Lightweight module that creates a namespaced test harness inside the customer's monitoring tenant or a dedicated observability namespace for the canary.
   - Components created (conditionally):
     * k8s namespace + test pod/service (simple app that emits metrics, traces, and logs)
     * prometheus ServiceMonitor / crd if using kube-prometheus. If remote-write-only deployments, push a dummy pushgateway or use OTLP -> remote_write adapter.
     * grafana datasource + temp dashboard import (optional) for smoke rendering.
     * otel-collector configmap + deployment (single replica) wired to local collector endpoint for test pod to push.
     * log-forwarder stub (fluent-bit) configured to ship to the stack's log sink.
   - Module inputs (common):
     * observability_namespace (string) — where to create test objects
     * enable_grafana_tests (bool)
     * enable_log_tests (bool)
     * prometheus_mode (enum: in-cluster | remote-write | hosted)
     * otel_endpoint (string)
     * log_sink_type (enum: s3|kafka|http)
     * alert_test_webhook (string) — test endpoint that records received alerts
     * ttl_hours (number) — auto-cleanup time for canary resources

2) Canary test pod (test-app):
   - Very small binary (go) or python script that:
     * exposes /metrics with a few counter/gauge/time-series that can be toggled via HTTP (/flip-alert, /emit-error-log, /emit-trace)
     * writes structured logs to stdout to validate log parsing rules (json fields to match grok/pipeline)
     * sends OTLP traces to localhost:4317 (simulating integrated apps)
   - Test scenarios:
     a) Metrics ingestion: create a unique metric name with a run-id label and verify Prometheus shows series within 60s.
     b) Alert fire: flip pattern that should trigger an existing rule; confirm the alert hits alert_test_webhook.
     c) Dashboard render: import a dashboard referencing the run-id metric; use grafana render endpoint (or simple panel health check) to confirm templating works.
     d) Log path: emit structured logs and confirm they reach log sink (S3 prefix or kafka topic).
     e) OTEL path: emit a short span; confirm it appears in tracing backend (tempo/jaeger).

3) Test runner (local CLI or CI job):
   - Sequence: tf apply canary module -> wait for resources -> run scenario steps -> collect artifacts -> tf destroy (if ttl not set)
   - Failure modes are non-blocking by default, but runner will return non-zero and upload artifacts when any check fails.
   - Runner should be able to run inside customer CI with minimal perms (namespace-level).

Terraform module notes (implementation details / caveats):
- Support for two deployment models: k8s native (ServiceMonitors + CRDs) and remote-write + OTLP pipeline. Module should detect prometheus_mode and create the right resources.
- Keep module strictly namespace-scoped where possible (avoid clusterrole bindings unless explicitly allowed).
- For customers that are air‑gapped, module must support local image registry references and skip any grafana/datasource provisioning that hits internet.
- Provide a boolean var: allow_cluster_role (default false) — when true create ServiceMonitor and PrometheusRule resources, else fall back to a push-based verification path.
- Outputs: canary_run_id, test_dashboard_uid, test_pod_logs_url (if centralized logs available), prometheus_query_example. All outputs are strings.
- Edge: some private deployments run Prometheus with sharding/federation — the module should support a query delay window (configurable). Default window=120s.

OTEL Collector notes (canary-focused pipeline snippet):
- Collector receives OTLP from test-pod and forwards to: 
  - prometheus receiver (metrics) -> prometheus exporter (if running in a mode to expose metrics locally for Prom scraping) OR
  - prometheus_remote_write exporter -> central prometheus if remote-write enabled
  - zipkin/jaeger/tempo exporters -> tracing backend
  - file/log exporter -> local file for log path smoke validations (useful for airgapped)
- Provide recommended resource limits for canary collector: cpu 100m, mem 128Mi. Single replica is fine for tests.
- Provide an example configmap template and a note to mount TLS certs when talking to external backends.

Prometheus specifics (checks & PromQL examples):
- Basic sanity queries: up{job="canary-test"} , rate(canary_requests_total[1m])
- Alert simulation: create ephemeral PrometheusRule with an alert that fires if canary_error_count > 0 for 30s. Use run-id label so we can filter.
- For remote-write setups, the verifier will: write to OTLP -> wait (120s) -> run a query via the control plane promql API (if available) or fetch from an observability API that exposes metrics. If neither available, the module emits a diagnostic bundle and flags "remote_write_unverifiable" so SRE can follow-up.

Grafana checks:
- Use grafana API (basic auth/api key) to:
  - create a new datasource pointing at the prometheus endpoint available to grafana (or use existing datasource alias), - import a small dashboard JSON (template provided in module), - call /render or /api/search/panels to ensure panels report no errors.
- For private deployments with no grafana provisioning API access, fallback to a manual checklist for operators (see checklist section).

Log shipping tests:
- Emit 10 json logs with unique id and severity levels. Verify via sink:
  - S3: list objects in prefix canary/<run-id>/ and grep for id
  - Kafka: tail topic (consumer) and confirm messages-> use consumer group canary-verify
  - HTTP: call test callback endpoint with ack from sink proxy
- Note: retention/partitioning may cause delay; use a longer window (5–10m) for large clusters. Document timeouts as variables.

Rollout / upgrade playbook (for observability component upgrades):
- Pre-upgrade: run canary suite (baseline_run_id) and store artifacts (metrics, logs, traces, grafana state).
- Upgrade step: upgrade chart/tf module controlling OTEL/Prom/Grafana.
- Post-upgrade: run canary suite again (compare run ids: baseline vs post).
- Compare checks: metrics available, alert behaviour consistent (if baseline fired an alert, post should as well), dashboards render, log path intact.
- If any critical check fails (metrics ingestion, alerting path, log egress), trigger automatic rollback policy if supported by release-engineering, else pages SRE on-call.

Artifacts and troubleshooting tips (what to collect on failure):
- test-pod logs (kubectl logs)
- otel-collector configmap + collector logs
- ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor objects and endpoints
- Prometheus rules and last 5 scrape logs for the target
- Grafana provisioning logs and dashboard JSON
- Example PromQL queries and raw responses
- If remote-write: show remote_write queue length/last success time from the TSDB remote write stats endpoint

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we want the canary module to auto-provision a test pagerduty integration or just provide a webhook to a staging PD/relay? (Prefer webhook only)
- Should we support non-k8s VM-based private deployments for the canary? (High value for onprem non-k8s customers — add as follow-up)
- Level of privileges module should assume in customer clusters (namespace only vs cluster role).
- How aggressive is tf destroy by default? Provide ttl_hours with a default of 24.

Next steps / TODOs
- [ ] Push initial module scaffold in terraform-modules repo (PR linked above).
- [ ] Build tiny test-app container image (go app) and publish to internal registry with airgap tags.
- [ ] Add grafana dashboard JSON and panel smoke tests.
- [ ] Create CI job template (github actions) that runs the canary module against a test VPC.
- [ ] Documentation: Confluence guide for operators + example runbook entry.

Notes from pairing session (2026-01-28):
- Aarti suggested adding an option to emit metrics via StatsD for legacy stacks. Add var: metrics_protocol = [prometheus|statsd|otlp].
- Ravi: prefer collector in sidecar vs shared instance? For canary single pod, sidecar costs more but isolates tests — add boolean sidecar_mode.
- Sofia: For remote-write only customers, provide a "verification agent" that scrapes the remote-write target via the control plane API rather than relying on in-cluster PromQL.

Contact for follow-up: eng-private-deployments channel on Slack (#eng-private-deployments) and Michael Chen (owner).

Quick run example (commands):
- terraform init && terraform apply -var='observability_namespace=canary-tests' -var='ttl_hours=2'
- watcher: ./canary-runner --run-id=$(output.canary_run_id) --verify  (runner will call pods /emit endpoints and check webhooks)

This doc should be treated as a living draft. Aim to keep module namespace-scoped by default, minimize cluster-wide perms, and make it simple for customers to run the important checks before/after upgrades.
